metadata.title: Claude, Closing Checklist.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude applies its own legal judgment to build a closing checklist, or follows a written instruction file, using the closing-checklist skill's own folder/SKILL.md/Steps structure as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that the skill runs the steps written in its SKILL.md, the same way every time -- not legal judgment, and nothing the file doesn't say.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (a step not written in the SKILL.md's Steps section stays a dashed, unconnected card; asking for it doesn't make it run)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude just knows how to build a legal closing checklist, straight from its own judgment. It doesn't — it reads one written file, step by step. So does Claude just read how to build it?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Does Claude just know how to build a closing checklist?', hesitates on 'know', corrects to 'read', lands the real question

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('know' -> 'read') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is closing-checklist, and it holds a single file: SKILL.md — the whole instruction set, in plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads the file, then acts. The file is the program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon labelled closing-checklist/, one file card SKILL.md inside it

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon labelled 'closing-checklist/' draws in on cream. Inside it, a single file card, 'SKILL.md', fades in with a small accent border -- one file total. The folder and file hold still while a caption lands beneath: 'the file is the program.'

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in the file's Steps section. Claude reads each step in order, and runs it — linear, no branching unless a step says so. If a step is written there, it runs. If it isn't, it doesn't exist.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- three step cards lighting up in order inside a Steps box; a dashed unconnected card sitting apart, outside it

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- linear, and only what's written
production_viz.mechanic: A box labelled 'SKILL.md -> Steps' holds three cards -- Step 1, Step 2, Step 3 -- connected left to right by arrows. Each lights up in turn as a read-head passes over it, left to right, strictly in order. THE ANCHOR. Off to the side, outside the box, a fourth card draws in dashed and gray, labelled only '?', unconnected to the arrow chain. It never lights up. A caption lands beneath: 'linear. no branching unless a step says so.' THIS EXACT DASHED CARD RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Ask for a step that's written in the file, and it runs the same way every time — reliable, because it's spec, not judgment. Ask for something the file never mentions, and nothing fills the gap: that step just isn't part of the run.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the three step cards run again in the same order; the dashed card gets an 'ask' arrow and stays dark

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- same steps, and the gap that stays a gap
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 SEQUENCE RETURNS: the same three-card Steps box, the read-head passing over Step 1, 2, 3 in the same order, each lighting teal -- labelled 'same input -> same output'. Beside it, the same dashed '?' card from B02 reappears. An arrow labelled 'ask' points into it. The card does not light; it stays dashed and gray. A line of small italic text appears beneath it: 'not written here. doesn't run.' A final caption at the bottom reads 'spec, not judgment.'

beats.narration_text: closing-checklist runs the steps written in its SKILL.md, the same way every time — not legal judgment, and nothing the file doesn't say.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I'm closing a transaction and want to use the closing-checklist skill. Read the SKILL.md and walk me through each step you'll run, in order, before you run any of them. That order matters — it's the whole spec, laid out before a single step executes. Liam, in for Bear.
